subject: Cognitive Science
title: Imitation and Social Learning
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: Imitation and Social Learning.

hook.text: A newborn sticks out her tongue when an adult does. At forty minutes old, she's already copying.

buildup.text: Imitation is the earliest social learning tool. Babies mirror expressions, sounds, and gestures.

discovery.text: By fourteen months, children imitate intended actions—not just performed ones. They read goals.

twist.text: Children over-imitate: they copy pointless steps even when they see the steps are unnecessary.

climax.text: Over-imitation may transmit culture—rituals and traditions that seem pointless but carry meaning.

quiz.question: What is over-imitation?
options: Copying unnecessary steps an adult performed
